inspiration.observed_pattern: MICROSECOND extracts fractional-second precision from quoted temporal values and numeric datetime forms.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Re-authored as a deterministic shipment-timing audit over DATETIME(6) and TIME(6) columns, covering distinct fractional precision, exact seconds, and NULL propagation with ordered CASE classification.

fixture_notes: Fixed temporal literals isolate MICROSECOND results for a six-digit fraction, a shorter fractional value normalized by MariaDB, an exact-second value, and missing timestamps.
determinism_notes: All temporal values are fixed literals; statements use a primary-key ordering and no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE shipment_ticks (tick_id INT PRIMARY KEY, tick_label VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL, observed_at DATETIME(6) NULL, elapsed TIME(6) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT tick_id, tick_label, observed_at, elapsed, MICROSECOND(observed_at) AS observed_microseconds, MICROSECOND(elapsed) AS elapsed_microseconds, CASE WHEN observed_at IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN MICROSECOND(observed_at) = 0 THEN 'whole-second' WHEN MICROSECOND(observed_at) < 100000 THEN 'short-fraction' ELSE 'precise-fraction' END AS precision_class FROM shipment_ticks ORDER BY tick_id

checks.sql: SELECT tick_id, MICROSECOND(observed_at) AS observed_microseconds, MICROSECOND(elapsed) AS elapsed_microseconds FROM shipment_ticks ORDER BY tick_id
